purpose: Structured doctrine source for scripts/_infra/session_briefing.py. Externalizes the previously-hardcoded briefing sections (closures by evidence class, do-not-test list, surviving/retired anomalies, weakly-testable and waiting-list bins, pitfalls) so the briefing script is a renderer+validator over an auditable registry rather than a wall of inline strings. This file does NOT introduce any new research claim: every entry restates content that was already embedded in the script and is sourced to docs/elimination_tiers.md, docs/claims_registry.json, memory/, or kernel constants. If an entry conflicts with docs/claims_registry.json (the canonical claims registry), that file wins. Evidence-class semantics are deliberately conservative: only mathematical_proof / structural_proof entries may be rendered with permanent / never language; exhaustive, sampled, empirical, and admissibility entries are scope-limited.

claims.statement: Autokey + arbitrary transposition cannot reach 24/24 FOR PRIMER LENGTH <= 25. [RESCOPED 2026-08-25, e_crib_35_autokey_peel_correction] The original result covered only the substitution-outer peel. In the transposition-outer peel, CT = Transpose(Autokey(PT)), PT[q] depends only on primer[q mod m] and the crib problem separates exactly. Measured: CT-autokey max 7/24 over 75 transpositions (STRONGER than the registered 21/24, elimination holds). PT-autokey max 23/24 for primer <= 25 (elimination holds) but 24/24 AT PRIMER 26, where 26 free letters face 24 cribs in 23 residue classes. So 'cannot reach 24/24' is FALSE at primer 26 and the permanent classification is rescoped to primer <= 25. The primer-26 case is UNDERDETERMINED, not a lead. The figure 'PT-autokey max=16/24' was wrong.
claims.scope: PT/CT autokey x Vig/Beau x arbitrary transposition
claims.retest_rule: never — structural ceiling below crib requirement

claims.statement: Stehle constant-difference (pos 55-63, 0-indexed): five consecutive equal lag-4 differences. RECOMPUTED 2026-08-25: under a uniform null the natural search 'a run of >=5 equal lag-L differences anywhere in the text, any lag 1-30' has p = 1/205 (200k trials); restricted to lag 1-24 it is 1/234. The previously cited p~1/642 was generous by about 3x. At the specific lag 4 alone it is 1/5,714, but lag 4 was found by inspection, not pre-registered, so the any-lag figure governs. Real pattern, weak evidence: local coincidence, not a mechanism.
claims.retest_rule: not a solution path; descriptive anomaly only
